_handoff.scopeNote: Official-source pass for LPG connection transfer, address change and distributor portability in Bengaluru, Karnataka. Current public IndianOil, HP Gas and Bharatgas material and Ministry/PIB public material were read without login, OTP, CAPTCHA, lookup, upload, payment, personal data or submission.
_handoff.observationNote: IndianOil and HP Gas publish carrier-specific transfer branches; Bharatgas publishes a current portability page with a login boundary; the Ministry/PIB release is government policy context and is older than the carrier pages. These materials must not be collapsed into one universal OMC procedure.
limitations: No OMC account, distributor lookup, connection number, address, OTP, document upload, payment, transfer request or case outcome was used.
No reviewed current public source establishes which distributor serves a particular Bengaluru address, whether a particular transfer will be approved, or a case-specific processing time.
Carrier terminology differs: IndianOil uses SV/TTV/TSV/TV, while HP Gas uses SV/e-CTA/TV; these are not interchangeable requirements.

The Ministry/PIB portability release was published in 2021 and is retained as government policy context, not as proof that every current Bengaluru portal or app route still behaves exactly as described.

claims.text: IndianOil's current Indane FAQ says that when a customer shifts within the same distributor's operating area, the customer should advise the distributor of the new address with supporting residence proof so the distributor changes its records and future supplies go to the new residence.
claims.notes: Carrier-specific public guidance. It does not identify the assigned Bengaluru distributor or guarantee acceptance of a supplied proof document.

claims.text: IndianOil's current Indane FAQ says that for a same-town move outside the present distributor's service area, the old distributor prepares a TTV against the original SV, and the receiving distributor uses proof of residence, TTV and DGCC booklet to prepare a TSV and provide a new consumer number.
claims.notes: IndianOil terminology and sequence only; do not substitute HP Gas e-CTA or BPCL portability language. The FAQ is not a live Bengaluru transaction.

claims.text: IndianOil's current Indane FAQ says that an out-of-town move requires surrender of the cylinder and regulator to the current distributor, who prepares a TV and refunds the equipment deposit; the customer is directed to a distributor at the new place for future service.
claims.notes: Carrier-specific published guidance; no equipment was surrendered and no refund or destination distributor was observed.

claims.text: HP Gas's current FAQ says that for a transfer within the city or certain adjoining city, the existing distributor issues an e-CTA/authorisation code against the SV, the e-CTA is valid for three months, and the customer presents the SV and code to the new distributor; cylinder and regulator need not be surrendered.
claims.notes: HPCL's carrier-specific rule. It is not evidence that another OMC uses e-CTA or that a supplied address is within the relevant city/market.

claims.text: HP Gas's current FAQ says that for an out-of-town transfer, the current distributor issues a TV and refunds the SV deposit after surrender of cylinders and regulator; the TV is valid for one year, and the Domestic Gas Consumer Card should be retained for endorsement at the new location.
claims.notes: HPCL carrier guidance; no surrender, TV, refund, endorsement or reconnection was attempted.

claims.text: HP Gas's current FAQ says KYC is required in cases including transfer of connection and change of name after the connection holder's death.
claims.notes: The FAQ does not establish a universal current proof list for every transfer case; no KYC was submitted.

claims.text: HPCL's public LPG systemic-improvements page says its portability feature can transfer an HP Gas connection to another distributor when the consumer changes residence within the city or is dissatisfied with the current distributor, and that requests can only be logged through the HP Gas Consumer Portal or HPPAY with OTP validation.
claims.notes: Current HPCL carrier description. The login/OTP boundary was recorded without attempting authentication.

claims.text: The current Bharatgas portability page says consumers may choose a nearby distributor or change distributor for service dissatisfaction only under a scheme available in selected cities, with no transfer fee or additional security deposit, and that login with a user ID and password is required.
claims.notes: Current BPCL page does not identify the selected-city list or establish that Bengaluru is enabled; no login or request was attempted.

claims.text: The Bharatgas customer declaration says that whenever the customer changes residence, the LPG distributor is to be informed in writing in advance for change of address in the records.
claims.notes: A Bharatgas customer undertaking, not a universal rule for IndianOil or HP Gas and not proof that a written request will be accepted in a particular case.

claims.text: The Bharatgas customer declaration says the customer encloses a completed KYC form with proof of address and proof of identity and accepts household/de-duplication conditions for a domestic subsidized connection.
claims.notes: The declaration does not provide a case-specific current checklist or approval decision; no identity or address data was supplied.

claims.text: The official Bharatgas unified transfer/regularization form lists Type A family transfer, Type B outside-family transfer, Type C transfer without transferor consent, Type D next-of-kin transfer after death and Type E regularization where equipment is held without the subscription voucher.
claims.notes: Blank BPCL form categories are published form content; they do not establish eligibility, distributor acceptance, fee or approval.

claims.text: A Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas PIB release dated 2021-06-10 lists OMC portals and mobile apps as channels for LPG portability, transfer of connection and address change for Indane, Bharatgas and HP Gas.
claims.notes: Government policy/public communication, not a current carrier page. Current OMC implementation and Bengaluru availability remain carrier-specific.

claims.text: The same 2021 Ministry/PIB release says online portability lets a customer using a registered login choose a distributor from the list serving the customer's area, and that the facility is free of transfer charges.
claims.notes: This is dated Ministry policy context and should not override a carrier's current selected-city, login, OTP or service-area constraints.

claims.text: The same 2021 Ministry/PIB release says the source distributor may contact the customer and the portability request may be withdrawn within three days; otherwise the connection transfers automatically to the target distributor.
claims.notes: Dated government release; no current portal timer, withdrawal control or automatic transfer was observed.

claims.text: The reviewed official material does not establish the current OMC/distributor assigned to a particular Bengaluru address, whether that address is inside a chosen distributor's service area or portability cluster, the accepted proof variant for a case, a current transfer fee/security amount for every branch, or approval/timing for a supplied connection.
claims.notes: No login, OTP, distributor lookup, upload, payment, equipment handoff or submission was performed.

roadblocks.title: Carrier and service-area boundary is case-specific
roadblocks.symptom: The same move can follow an address update, a same-town voucher/e-CTA transfer, an out-of-town TV route or an authenticated portability route.
roadblocks.likelyCause: OMC terminology and distributor coverage differ; public pages do not assign a supplied Bengaluru address.
roadblocks.recovery: Identify the current OMC and distributor through its official current channel, then confirm the new address's serving area before choosing a branch.

roadblocks.title: Online portability stops at authenticated access
roadblocks.symptom: HP Gas requires user login and OTP; Bharatgas requires user ID/password and limits the scheme to selected cities.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Portability is an account-bound OMC service rather than an unauthenticated public lookup.
roadblocks.recovery: Use only the relevant OMC's official account route if the consumer elects to proceed; no credentials or OTP were collected in this pass.
